entries.finding: A 2025 systematic review and meta-analysis of 13 randomized trials found ginseng supplementation significantly improved flow-mediated dilation, a measure of endothelial function.
The same pooled analysis found a significant increase in endothelium-derived nitric oxide levels with ginseng supplementation.
The 2025 meta-analysis found a significant reduction in pulse wave velocity with ginseng, consistent with an improvement in the measured marker of arterial stiffness.
No statistically significant pooled effect was observed for augmentation index, showing that vascular findings were not uniformly positive across all measures.
A separate 2025 GRADE-assessed meta-analysis of 44 randomized trials reported a significant reduction in IL-6 with ginseng supplementation, suggesting a possible anti-inflammatory signal.
The 2025 GRADE-assessed synthesis reported that ginseng may increase adiponectin, while emphasizing that further well-designed long-term trials are warranted.
The 2025 GRADE-assessed meta-analysis found no significant effect of ginseng on body weight, BMI, or waist circumference, arguing against a generalized weight-loss claim.

A 2025 systematic review of 11 randomized clinical trials found chamomile was associated with a statistically significant reduction in mucositis severity, although the authors called for larger trials.
The chamomile review found a significant pooled reduction in pain severity in a four-study sub-analysis, with no observed statistical heterogeneity in that subset.
Three randomized studies in the 2025 chamomile synthesis showed a significant reduction in mucosal inflammation, with no statistical heterogeneity in that small subset.
The pooled analysis of five randomized studies did not find a statistically significant antimicrobial effect for chamomile, and heterogeneity was high.
Three randomized studies showed no significant pooled effect of chamomile on gingival index, with substantial heterogeneity.
